subject.title: plugins.entries.<id>.subagent.allowModelOverride is ignored for interactive (client-scoped) subagent runs

question: Should the shipped `plugins.entries.<id>.subagent.allowModelOverride` grant authorize plugin subagent provider/model overrides from interactive client-scoped contexts?
rationale: Current SDK docs imply the opt-in applies generally, but shipped config help and runtime behavior scoped it to background fallback runs, so this is a real compatibility and authorization-boundary choice.

options.title: Approve Widened Grant
options.body: Land or revise the linked PR so explicit plugin-scoped subagent trust applies in background and client-scoped contexts, bounded by `allowedModels` and non-transitive internal authority.

options.title: Keep Background-Only
options.body: Reject runtime widening and update SDK docs plus runtime errors so operators know this config key cannot authorize interactive plugin subagent overrides.

options.title: Split Scoped Contexts
options.body: Cover interactive operator-scoped plugin runs while explicitly excluding external plugin HTTP route scopes if maintainers want that boundary preserved.

recommendation.title: Approve Widened Grant
recommendation.body: Land or revise the linked PR so explicit plugin-scoped subagent trust applies in background and client-scoped contexts, bounded by `allowedModels` and non-transitive internal authority.

likelyOwner.reason: jalehman introduced the trusted plugin subagent override policy and has the strongest feature-history signal for the config-contract decision.
